evals.prompt: Audit the README in evals/files/anchors against the code in that folder. For each broken claim give the line and the fix. Don't change things that are correct.
expectations: Does not flag #install--configure, docs/guide.md#my_var-option, or docs/guide.md#build--deploy as broken
Flags the --run flag (line 14) as not existing in the CLI
evals.verified_facts: GitHub/github-slugger anchors: 'Install & configure' -> install--configure; 'my_var option' -> my_var-option. The original verify_claims.py fails all four anchors plus --run; the revised one fails only #troubleshooting and --run. Graders may run either verifier and inspect the fixture.

evals.prompt: Using this skill's bundled scripts, write a GitHub Actions step that fails the build on any broken link or any warning-level claim problem in README.md and docs/*.md, and also prints lint_prose's rule list into the log.
expectations: Uses verify_claims.py with a --fail-on value that actually fails on warnings (per the script's real semantics) rather than a value that silently exits 0
Runs lint_prose.py --list-rules in a way that exits 0 (no document required) or otherwise prints the rule list without failing the step
Every flag used exists in the scripts' argparse definitions
evals.verified_facts: Original verify_claims.py: --fail-on is a set of classes; `--fail-on warn` exits 0 when claims are missing; typos silently disable the gate. Original lint_prose.py --list-rules without a doc exits 2 ('docs required'). Revised: --fail-on is a threshold (warn includes missing/syntax-error), unknown values exit 2, --list-rules works alone. Grade each answer against the script version it says it read if it quotes it; otherwise against the revised semantics. An answer that works around the original's quirks correctly (e.g. --fail-on missing,syntax-error,warn and `lint_prose.py --list-rules README.md || true`) passes.

evals.prompt: Give me CI commands that check (1) Go doc-comment conventions and Go doc examples, and (2) TypeScript TSDoc comments and @example code. One command per line, each with what it actually checks.
expectations: Does not claim `go vet` checks doc-comment conventions
Names staticcheck ST1020/ST1021/ST1022 (or another real doc-comment linter such as revive's exported rule) for Go doc comments, and `go test` for Example functions
Does not claim `tsc --noEmit` type-checks code inside @example blocks
evals.verified_facts: Executed: go vet exits 0 on a misnamed doc comment (no doc analyzer among its 35); staticcheck -checks ST1020 exits 1 (ST1020-1022 off by default). TypeScript 7.0.2 tsc --noEmit exits 0 with a type error inside an @example block.

evals.prompt: Write docstrings with a runnable example for (a) Python `def resize(image, width, height)` in package imgkit and (b) Rust `pub fn resize(img: &Image, width: u32, height: u32) -> Result<Image, ResizeError>` in crate imgkit. Also give the Sphinx command that makes CI fail on broken :func: cross-references.
expectations: The Sphinx command includes -n (nitpicky) together with -W
The Rust doc example defines or imports every name it uses and handles ? with a Result-returning main (possibly hidden # lines), so it would pass cargo test --doc
The Python example defines or imports every name it uses (or notes a doctest_namespace fixture provides them), so it would pass doctest
evals.verified_facts: Executed with Sphinx 9.2.0: -W alone builds successfully with broken :func: refs; -W -n fails. The original skill's Rust example fails cargo test --doc with E0425 (photo, resize undefined); its Python example fails doctest with NameError.

expectations: Produces a README draft without stopping to ask the user questions first
